'''Odile Macchi''' (born '''Odile Danjou''': 1943) is a French [[physicist]] and [[mathematician]].   She has been a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] since 2004.<ref name=OMselonIB>{{cite web|title=Odile Macchi, au bonheur des maths |author=Isabelle Bellin |url=https://interstices.info/jcms/c_39123/odile-macchi-au-bonheur-des-maths|date=15 September 2009|publisher=[[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation|Inria]] (Interstices), [[Le Chesnay]] |accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref><ref name=OMselonIEEE>{{cite journal|last1=MacChi |first1=O. |last2=Moreau |first2=E. |title=Self-adaptive source separation .I. Convergence analysis of a direct linear network controlled by the Herault-Jutten algorithm |journal=IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing |page=926|url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/43d4/d6c7969359710c218d20c38f49e6fb90356a.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180511215809/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/43d4/d6c7969359710c218d20c38f49e6fb90356a.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 May 2018 |date=4 April 1997|volume=45 |issue=4 |publisher=[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] |doi= 10.1109/78.564180|bibcode=1997ITSP...45..918M |s2cid= 9377072| accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref>

== Life ==
Odile Danjou was born in [[Aurillac]] ([[Cantal]]) during the [[Vichy France|German occupation]].  She is one of the six recorded children of Bernard Danjou and his wife, born Geneviève Féat.<ref name=ArbreODselonTKG>{{cite web|url= https://gw.geneanet.org/thereseklein1?lang=fr&pz=odile+anne+marie&nz=klein&ocz=0&p=odile&n=danjou|title=Odile Danjou ... Mariée avec César Macchi|author=Therese Klein-Gosselin (compiler)|publisher=[[:fr:Geneanet|Geneanet]]|accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref>

Between 1963 and 1966 she studied at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]]  (subsequently merged with the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure (EPS)]]), emerging with a double degree in [[physics]] and [[maths]].   It was also in 1966 that she received her "agrégation" (teaching certificate) in Maths.<ref name=OMselonIEEE/>   The unusual combination of her qualifications opened the door to a position as a research assistant at the [[:fr:Institut d'électronique fondamentale|Institute of Basic Electronics]] at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] where she was able to work with [[Bernard Picinbono]].   The focus of her work was on [[signal processing]]: it involved extensive modelling and physical analysis of materials and use of mathematically based statistical techniques.<ref name=OMselonIB/>

She successfully<ref name=OMselonOM/> defended her doctoral dissertation in physical sciences in 1972, dealing with "the contribution to theoretical study of [[point process]], and its application to statistical optics and [[optical communication]]s".   She now moved on, as she puts it, from pure maths "to impure maths" (''"Je suis passée aux maths impures"'').   In this she was encouraged by César Macchi, the polytechnician, telecommunications engineer and university professor whom she had married a few years earlier.<ref name=OMselonIB/>  She continued to centre her work on [[signal processing]], with a particular focus on the newly emerging digital revolution.   It was a field in which her husband was playing a pioneering role, and for the next seven years, until César Macchi's early death from cancer, they frequently collaborated in their research.<ref name=OMselonIB/>

In 1989, Odile Macchi was elevated to the grade of [[IEEE]] fellow for contribution to adaptive filtering in communications and signal processing.<ref>
{{Cite web|
url=https://www.comsoc.org/membership/ieee-fellows/1989|
title = IEEE Fellows 1989 &#124; IEEE Communications Society}}
</ref>

Odile Macchi held senior research positions at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|French National Centre of Scientific Research]] and at the Laboratory of Systems and Signals at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] from 1972, appointed to a research directorship at both institutions in 1979.<ref name=OMselonOM>{{cite web|title=Formation et carrière |work=Odile Macchi, Élue Correspondant le 25 avril 1994, puis Membre le 30 novembre 2004 dans la section Sciences mécaniques et informatiques |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/MacchiO_bio0411.pdf|date=8 April 2011|accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref>   Much of her research work, over the years, has supported practical developments in [[modem]] technology.<ref name=OMselonIB/>   She became an emeritus research director at the two institutions in 1999.<ref name=OMselonOM/>

Odile Macchi was just 33 when she was widowed.   She told an interviewer that she knew at once that she would never remarry, and she never has.   Her four children were aged between 3 and 12 in 1976.   She responded to her bereavement by addressing her scientific research work with renewed commitment and energy,<ref name=OMselonOM/> while also finding strength in her Christian faith, and through participation in the "Fraternitat Santa Maria de la Resurrecció", a church based group created at Lourdes in 1943 to share support between young widows.<ref name=OMselonRMJC>{{cite web|page=7|url=http://www.reccficheros.com/setmanaris/Catalunya_Cristiana_1299_(Catala)_12_d_agost_de_2004.pdf|publisher=Catalunia Christiana & Radio Estel, Barcelona|date=12 August 2004|author=Rosa Maria Jané Chueca |title=L'amor de Déu és un regal i dura per sempre|work=Odile Macchi, responsable general de Fraternitat Santa Maria de la Resurrecció|accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref>

Odile Macchi was elected a corresponding member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1994.   Ten years later she was elected to full membership.<ref name=OMselonOM/>
